#  * DI tags do NOT carry rule or channel names in this tree: the only tag matching
#    addTag('qmx.*') is ContainerFactory.php:154, a collector-configuration tag.
#    So the tag mechanism, though named as a hazard, does not bite here.
# What no probe of ANY shape can cover, stated as a limit rather than a finding:
#  a producer name supplied by a user's own qmx.yaml under computed_metrics.  After
#  the split it is user data, so it exists in no tracked file by construction, and
#  the only defence is the fail-closed registry check the plan already requires.
# ============ SUBJECT H: DOES THE LOUD REFUSAL IT NEEDS ALREADY EXIST? ============
# Asked because the brief asks it directly.  Measured answer: NO.
# Four grammars accept a directive target today, and not one of them admits a colon:
#     PATTERN, target class [\w.*-] - neither '#' nor ':' is admitted.
# So a 'channel:level' target does not parse today; it cannot be REFUSED because it
# is not even RECOGNISED - the regex simply stops at the colon and the remainder
# falls into the free-text reason group.  Two seams exist where the refusal could
# live, and neither does the job:
#     for configuration and CLI exclusion keys, never for an inline directive.
#     validate() EMITS a finding (annotation.unresolved-directive) - a report entry,
#     not a refusal, and it is reached only for a target that already parsed.
# Consequence for the plan: Sh5's 'one place of loud refusal for an impossible
# channel:level pair' is NEW code, not an edit to an existing check, and it has to
# be reachable from BOTH seams above or the two directive families disagree.
